import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.formula.api import ols

# Load the dataset
invaded_niche = pd.read_csv('/data/invaded_niche_pathways.csv')

# Display the first few rows of the dataset
invaded_niche.head()

# Check for missing values
invaded_niche.isnull().sum()

# Check the data types
invaded_niche.dtypes

# Perform a correlation analysis between 'n.gard' and other variables
correlation_matrix = invaded_niche.corr()
correlation_matrix['n.gard']

# Perform a multiple regression analysis to identify significant interactions
model = ols('n.gard ~ cropland.1956.50m + urban.1956.50m + cropland.1993.50m + urban.1993.50m + cropland.2009.50m + urban.2009.50m + progressive.1956.2009.50m + regressive.1956.2009.50m + no.changes.1956.2009.50m + progressive.1993.2009.50m + regressive.1993.2009.50m + no.changes.1993.2009.50m + distance.stream + distance.road + annual.temperature + annual.rainfall + annual.radiation', data=invaded_niche).fit()
anova_table = sm.stats.anova_lm(model, typ=2)
anova_table

import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.formula.api import ols

# Load the dataset with the correct delimiter

# Remove non-numeric columns or convert them to numeric if possible
numeric_columns = invaded_niche.select_dtypes(include=['number']).columns
invaded_niche_numeric = invaded_niche[numeric_columns]

# Perform a multiple regression analysis
model = ols('n.gard ~ n.total + n.unint + n.agfo + annual.temperature + elevation', data=invaded_niche_numeric).fit()
